passage:
I'm Nilesh, and no, Neelam, I haven't decided. Everyone keeps asking me that like there's a deadline.
Radhika told me in February that she never finished her degree. For a whole year she'd talked about exams, a convocation she "skipped", a certificate "in the post". None of it was real.
Some mornings I wake up so angry I can't eat. I think: who lies for a year to the person she's going to marry? I draft messages ending it.
And then by evening I remember her laughing at my terrible cooking, or how she sat with my mother in the hospital for two nights. And I miss her so badly it hurts in my chest.
Both are true. That's what nobody tells you. I'm furious and I still love her, sometimes in the same hour.
I've stopped trying to make one feeling win by Friday. I'm letting them both be there for now.

qa.q: What did Radhika say about her certificate?
qa.a: Radhika said it was "in the post".

qa.q: What is Nilesh feeling about Radhika?
qa.a: Nilesh feels betrayed and furious in the mornings, and deep love and longing by evening, swinging between the two within a single day.

qa.q: What wise choice has Nilesh made about the mixed feelings?
qa.a: Nilesh has stopped forcing a decision by a deadline and is letting both the anger and the love exist while things become clearer.

qa.q: How might Neelam feel hearing Nilesh's answer?
qa.a: Neelam might realise that asking whether Nilesh has decided adds pressure, and understand that there is no quick answer to give.

grounding: Nilesh, lied to for a year by Radhika, swings between anger and love for her and stops forcing a decision by any deadline.

passage:
I've shared a desk with Lakshmi at work for two years, so I watched this whole month from close up.
In October she found out her younger brother, Varun, had dropped out of college a year ago and pretended to be attending. She'd been paying half his fees.
On Monday she was furious. She slammed her drawer and said, "I'm not sending him a single rupee again."
On Wednesday, I saw her ordering a food parcel to his hostel.
On Friday she cried in the washroom and said, "I hate him. I miss him. How is that even possible?"
The next week she didn't answer his calls, then she called him at midnight.
I don't know what's going on inside her exactly. From the outside, it looks like love and anger taking turns.
I just told her she doesn't have to decide anything this week. She nodded, and for once her shoulders dropped.
Himani

qa.q: How long ago had Varun dropped out of college?
qa.a: Varun had dropped out a year ago.

qa.q: What does Lakshmi's "I hate him. I miss him." show about her feelings?
qa.a: It shows Lakshmi feels betrayed and angry at Varun's lie and still loves and misses him, both at once.

qa.q: Why was Himani's comment about not deciding this week helpful?
qa.a: It took away the pressure to resolve the mixed feelings quickly, which is why Lakshmi's shoulders finally dropped.

qa.q: How might Varun experience his sister's swings between silence and midnight calls?
qa.a: Varun might feel confused and anxious, not knowing where he stands, yet the calls and food parcel show him she has not given up on him.

grounding: Himani watches Lakshmi swing between anger and love for a brother who lied for a year, and tells her there is no need to decide yet.

passage:
I'm Chinmay, and my older brother Kamal lied to me for six months. He said he was still at the bank. He'd been let go in January. Every morning he put on his tie, left the house, and sat in a library until six.
When I found out, I shouted things I'd never said to anyone. I felt stupid and betrayed, as if our whole childhood had been a costume.
And an hour later I was in the kitchen making him tea, because his hands were shaking.
That's how it's been since. Some days I can't look at him. Some evenings we watch cricket and laugh like nothing happened, and then I feel angry at myself for laughing.
Our Amma says, "You don't have to decide by Diwali." I think she's right. I'm furious with him. I love him. Both are just true right now.

qa.q: Where did Kamal sit every day after leaving the house?
qa.a: In a library until six.

qa.q: What was Chinmay feeling after finding out?
qa.a: Chinmay felt betrayed and furious, yet an hour later was making tea for Kamal out of love.

qa.q: What does Amma's advice offer Chinmay?
qa.a: Permission not to settle it by a deadline, so both the anger and the love can be felt while things settle.

qa.q: What might those six months have been like for Kamal?
qa.a: Kamal was probably ashamed and scared, putting on a tie each morning to hide the job loss, and shaking once it came out.

grounding: Shows a person who loves a brother that lied swinging between betrayal and care, with no deadline to settle it.

passage:
Counsellor's note, Wednesday, individual session: Amandeep
Amandeep came alone today. Three weeks ago she found out her husband, Manoj, had hidden a large loan from her for over a year and lied when she asked about the missing statements.
She spoke fast. "I want to throw his things out of the window. And then I see him asleep and I want to pull the blanket over him." She laughed and cried in the same breath. She said she felt like a pendulum and asked me if something was wrong with her.
I told her nothing was wrong with her. Loving someone and feeling betrayed by them can sit side by side, and nobody has to make sense of it by a certain date.
What I did next: we made a short list of what she needs this week, not forever. She wants the full loan papers in her hand, and one evening with her sister. She agreed to come back next Wednesday.

qa.q: What did Manoj hide from Amandeep?
qa.a: A large loan, for over a year.

qa.q: How is Amandeep feeling, and what shows it?
qa.a: Amandeep feels torn between anger and love, wanting to throw Manoj's things out and then to pull the blanket over him, laughing and crying at once.

qa.q: What did the counsellor do that helped?
qa.a: Said nothing was wrong with Amandeep, that both feelings can sit together without a deadline, and helped list what she needs just this week.

qa.q: How might Manoj be affected by Amandeep's swings?
qa.a: Manoj may not know from hour to hour where he stands, which is part of the cost of the lie he told.

grounding: Shows a wife betrayed by her husband's hidden loan swinging between anger and love, told that both are real and need no deadline.

passage:
Thursday
Amandeep called again. I let it ring out, then stared at the phone for twenty minutes.
Five weeks ago I found out she hadn't missed my engagement because of "a family emergency". She went to a concert in Bengaluru. She posted a photo in a private story and forgot her cousin could see it.
We've been friends since we were nine. She held my hand at Papa's funeral. How can the same person lie to my face and then send me a crying voice note at midnight?
Some mornings I miss her so much I draft a long message. By lunch I'm angry again and delete it.
Today Mausi said, "You can love her and be angry. You don't have to pick one yet." It helped more than I expected.
Maybe tomorrow I'll call back. Or maybe next week. Both are okay.
Ganga

qa.q: Where did Amandeep actually go instead of the engagement?
qa.a: She went to a concert in Bengaluru.

qa.q: What was Ganga feeling while staring at the phone?
qa.a: Ganga felt torn, hurt and angry about the lie, yet missing a friend of many years.

qa.q: What did Mausi's words give Ganga?
qa.a: Permission to hold both love and anger without choosing yet, so Ganga can decide when to call back without a deadline.

qa.q: What might Amandeep be feeling, judging by her calls?
qa.a: Amandeep seems remorseful and anxious, calling again and sending a crying voice note at midnight.

grounding: Shows a person swinging between betrayal and love for a lifelong friend who lied, learning there is no deadline to resolve it.

passage:
Past midnight. Dhruv on the sofa, his wife Vandana in the bedroom, both awake.
Dhruv: I can't sleep
Vandana: me neither
Dhruv: six months. you told me you were at your mother's every Saturday
Vandana: I know. I was at the bank, sorting out Kunal's loans. I didn't want you to worry
Dhruv: I'd rather worry than be lied to
Dhruv: I'm so angry I can't look at you
Dhruv: and I also keep wanting to come into the other room and hug you. which makes me angrier
Vandana: you can feel both. I'm not asking you to pick
Dhruv: I don't know tonight if I'm staying in this marriage
Dhruv: sorry. that's not true either. I don't want to leave. I just don't know how to trust you
Vandana: I'll tell you everything, with the papers. whenever you're ready. no rush
Dhruv: not tonight
Dhruv: goodnight. I mean it, even angry

qa.q: Where did Vandana say she was every Saturday?
qa.a: At her mother's.

qa.q: What mix of feelings is Dhruv describing?
qa.a: Dhruv feels betrayed and so angry he can't look at Vandana, yet still wants to hug her, which makes him angrier.

qa.q: What does Vandana do that helps?
qa.a: She accepts both of his feelings without asking him to choose, offers to share everything with the papers, and says there is no rush.

qa.q: How might Vandana be feeling as she waits?
qa.a: Vandana likely feels guilty and afraid of losing Dhruv, but steady enough to give him time.

grounding: Shows a person who loves someone who lied, feeling betrayed and still wanting the relationship, swinging between both with no deadline to resolve it.
